clue.text: Prisoner given hearing — one has no alternative but to listen

definitions.text: one has no alternative but to listen

blocks.note: a prisoner is held captive
a formal hearing, as in an audience with the Pope

explanation.surface: A prisoner is granted a hearing and is told to sit still and listen.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive audience is a group of listeners who cannot leave, so they are forced to hear whatever is said.

clue.text: Administrative officer's publicity jaunt — about time!

indicators.note: about suggests letters turned and moved around into a new order

blocks.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
taken as written, to be mixed
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An exasperated note that an officer's PR trip is long overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive, matching the answer's 's: 'Adjutant's publicity...' reads naturally, so the 's belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is a military officer who assists a commander with administrative duties.

clue.text: Drivers in the forest

blocks.note: first meaning: golf clubs, the driver being the number one wood
second meaning: an area of trees

explanation.surface: Motorists have strayed into the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists, but in golf the long-hitting clubs are called woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Woods are a stretch of trees, so the word serves as a plural synonym for a forest; golf's driver is also a wood.

clue.text: Cereal containing half bran could make one brainy

indicators.note: half asks for only the front portion of the following word
containing means the first word holds the second inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, the outer word
the first two of four letters of bran

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal with added bran claims to make you clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral, from the Latin for brain, describes someone intellectual and given to thinking.

clue.text: One talks a lot about US fuel container

blocks.note: gas is American for petrol
a bag holds things

explanation.surface: Someone droning on about American petrol cans.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas is the American word for what Britons call petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is an informal word for a person who chatters endlessly.

clue.text: They say it's what a matador does that could be missed

indicators.note: they say points to how the phrase is spoken rather than written

blocks.note: a matador dodges the charging animal

explanation.surface: A remark about bullfighting: the matador's work is skipping out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something avoidable can be sidestepped or done without, so it could be missed.

clue.text: I finally get silver out for the creature

indicators.note: 'finally' keeps only the first letter of 'I'

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written
the letter I, placed at the end

explanation.surface: Someone at last brings out the silverware for an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' is not taking a last letter here; it tells you the I goes at the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a burrowing rodent of Central and South America, so it is a creature.

clue.text: Establishment's friend behaving according to its precepts

blocks.note: an establishment is an institution; the 's joins it to what follows
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend of the organisation who sticks to its rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting institutionally means acting in the manner of an organisation, following its established rules and norms.

clue.text: Dead Roman could be the daughter of Cassiopeia

indicators.note: could be hints the letters might form something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: Speculating whether a deceased Roman was a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Cassiopeia's boast led to her daughter being chained to a rock as a sea monster's sacrifice.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda was the princess, daughter of Cepheus and Cassiopeia, rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: For example, in the forefront with antipathy for animal products

indicators.note: in places the example phrase inside the word for the front

blocks.note: the van is the leading part, as in vanguard
e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: An example of someone leading the charge against animal products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the forefront' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the insertion signal and 'the' is filler.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan avoids all animal products, a stance the clue describes as antipathy towards them.

clue.text: Student turned around, about to move in a clumsy way

definitions.text: to move in a clumsy way

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are spun into a new order
about also suggests letters scattered and moved round

blocks.note: L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student spins round, about to stumble off awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To trundle is to move along slowly and heavily, like a cart on wheels.

clue.text: Bet quire's almost entirely recycled to make this fuel

indicators.note: almost entirely means all but the very end of the word is kept
recycled material is broken down and remade in a fresh form

blocks.note: taken as written
a quire is a set of sheets of paper; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A wager that a stack of paper will be recycled into fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Quire loses its last letter before the shuffle; the 's simply reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A briquet, or briquette, is a compressed block of coal dust or other material burned as fuel.

clue.text: Small container said to be disgusting

indicators.note: said means we go by the spoken form of the word

blocks.note: vile means disgusting

explanation.surface: A little pot that someone calls nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle for liquids such as medicine.

clue.text: Utilitarian prat bearing unnatural stigma

indicators.note: unnatural says the next word is in an abnormal, rearranged form
bearing means carrying something within

blocks.note: taken as written; a prat is a fool
taken as written, six letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A practical-minded fool carrying an odd mark of shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Prat is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A utilitarian, like a pragmatist, judges things by practical usefulness rather than principle.

clue.text: Certificate Conservative unknown got for negotiation

blocks.note: a diploma is a certificate of qualification
C abbreviates Conservative
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unknown Tory gained a qualification in bargaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomacy is the conduct of negotiations between parties, especially nations.

clue.text: Rise for the worker?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pay increase for an employee
setter's reading: a mound of earth made by the worker insect

explanation.walkthrough: A rise is British for a pay increase, but it is also a small hill; the worker is the insect caste in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker insects build a heap of soil over their nest, a little rise in the ground.

clue.text: European pet, one known for its offensive smell

definitions.text: one known for its offensive smell

blocks.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: A pet from the Continent that is notorious for stinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat, a weasel relative, releases a foul-smelling secretion when threatened.

clue.text: Pinochet changed, pronounced sound

definitions.note: read as 'sounded as pronounced', describing spelling that matches speech

indicators.note: changed tells us the dictator's name has altered form

blocks.note: taken as written; Pinochet was a Chilean dictator

explanation.surface: A former Chilean dictator's change is declared sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetic means relating to speech sounds, or spelt as it is pronounced.

clue.text: Cross Capone off crucial set up

indicators.note: off means taken away from the word that follows

blocks.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
taken as written
to fix is to rig or set up an outcome

explanation.surface: An angry Capone storms off after a vital frame-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for Capone's mood but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucifix is a cross bearing a figure of Christ.

clue.text: Stained loo creating despair?

indicators.note: creating implies the letters are worked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: A dirty toilet leaves someone in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolation is a state of bleak misery, close to despair; the question mark flags a looser fit.

clue.text: Working in digs by the railway

definitions.note: a description of where it lies rather than a strict synonym

indicators.note: working means set in motion, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: taken as written, six letters

explanation.surface: Someone works from lodgings beside the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A siding is a short stretch of track beside the main railway line, used for parking trains.

clue.text: Sign of approval when alien''s given permit to travel

blocks.note: a tick mark shows something is correct
ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: An alien gets the nod and a travel pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket is a document entitling the holder to make a journey.

clue.text: American car drives itself!

blocks.note: first meaning: US informal word for a motor car
second meaning: automatic, self-operating

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests a self-driving vehicle; the second sense is the automatic setting, as on a camera or gearbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is American slang for a car, and also short for automatic, meaning something that runs by itself.

clue.text: One giving rondo new twist

indicators.note: a new twist means the letters are wrung into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written; a rondo is a musical form

explanation.surface: A composer gives a rondo a fresh variation.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a person who donates, that is someone who gives money, blood or organs.

clue.text: Native at last destroyed mice

indicators.note: destroyed means broken apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: the end comes at last
taken as written, four letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Local mice finally wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' looks like it wants a final letter, but it is a synonym for the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic describes something native to, or naturally found only in, a particular area.

clue.text: Divorcee to return with an accountant for rare items

indicators.note: return means go back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse
the little word taken as written
an means one, written as the Roman numeral
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A divorced spouse comes back with a bookkeeper to claim the curios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An' standing for one, then I, is a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are unusual and striking things, especially from far-off places, so they are rare items.

clue.text: One doubting part of policy Nicaraguan advocated

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a stretch of letters inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word break

explanation.surface: A sceptic questions a piece of Nicaraguan policy that was promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic distrusts people's sincerity and motives, so is someone who doubts.

clue.text: Leader of ideal trio by arrangement

indicators.note: by arrangement means the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: The head of a perfect threesome, chosen by arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a person; in British newspapers a leader is the main opinion article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British journalism the leader, or leading article, is the newspaper's editorial.
